page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.4xlarge is a storage-oriented instance from the Local SSDs family, designed to provide high-capacity direct-attached storage alongside balanced compute resources. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are supplemented by 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core) and an integrated 1919 GB local SSD. It includes no dedicated GPUs and operates with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate typical mid-tier throughput for its processor generation. While single-threaded tests such as the Geekbench single-core score (964.0) and stress-ng single-core (1107.99) fall into the bottom quartile, multithreaded capabilities reach average metrics, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5912.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12984.68. Similarly, memory bandwidth yields 69.35 GB/sec for uncached 256MB block reads and 53.33 GB/sec for large block writes, aligning with mid-range operational metrics.

In operational benchmarks, the instance yields average figures across database and serving scenarios, executing 11.66 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining a static web serving throughput of 7.87 GB/sec. LLM inference shows adequate capability on lightweight models (820.54 prompt tokens/sec on a 135M model) but drops significantly on 7B parameter models (8.44 tokens/sec generation), reflecting the limitations of CPU-only execution without hardware acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server balances its older Skylake-era compute efficiency with high-density integrated local SSD capacity. Workloads that require extensive local caching, fast ephemeral read/write capability, relational databases, or distributed NoSQL deployments will derive the highest utility from the bundled 1919 GB SSD, whereas compute-bound or single-thread-sensitive tasks face performance tradeoffs.

Multi-core performance reaches middle-tier results with a PassMark CPU score of 12984.68 and Geekbench multi-core score of 5912.0, balanced against lower single-thread capabilities (964.0 Geekbench single-core).
